svg.title: Figure 1 — LC-TEM nanoparticle analysis pipeline
svg.text: Figure 1 | Pipeline architecture for crystallographic phase analysis of liquid-cell TEM nanoparticle videos
Every thumbnail is real data — frame 500 of the 053243 PtRu/TiO₂ series, at the corresponding stage of the pipeline
UMVD Denoiser — self-supervised, blind-frame temporal interpolation
self-supervised loss L = ‖ f( masked window ) − I t ‖² / 2
the target is the NOISY centre frame — the network never sees a clean reference, because none exists for a fluxional surface
registration runs on the band-passed frames; the smoothed shifts
are applied to the raw ones. Trajectory filtering is two-stage —
the median rejects registration spikes, Savitzky–Golay removes
jitter while preserving the slow physical drift.
replication padding throughout, no bias anywhere, ReLU activations.
Adam, lr 1e-3 halved every 10 epochs, 128² patches.
transfer ≈ fine-tune ≈ from-scratch on this data
the crop is centred on the mask CENTROID, not the bounding-box
centre — the centroid stays stable when the mask boundary flickers.
Frames with no admissible mask are dropped, which is why T shrinks
particle fills a constant fraction of every frame
a median (not a mean) suppresses isolated single-frame flips while
preserving a step — which is what a real phase change is. Inside an
Ih-family segment a second (drop-Ih→Dh) model decides:
p(Ih)>.6 ∧ p(Ih)>p(Dh)+.2 → Ih; mirror → Dh; else Ih→Dh
recovers the class a single frame cannot decide

Stages 1–3 are chained by pipeline.py; Stage 4 runs on the resulting crop stack. All four stages are self-supervised or pre-trained — the only hand-labelled data in the pipeline trains the Stage-4 classifier.
